rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT+U method (PBE functional, Hubbard U correction) applied to known TiO2 surfaces. However, constructing the (1×2)-reconstructed slab models (Onishi/Park) and correctly using the surface energy formula requires domain-specific care. No novel algorithm, but several interacting components (bulk, isolated atom, chemical potential, three slab models, DOS extraction).
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises ~5-6 distinct DFT calculations (bulk, O atom, three slab relaxations, two DOS computations) with dependencies and intermediate data. Setting up Quantum ESPRESSO with pseudopotentials and generating input files adds orchestration complexity, though each step is a well-defined quantum chemistry task.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces DFT+U surface free energies and gap state positions from a computational surface science paper. The method is standard PBE+U, but requires building slab models and running multiple geometry optimizations and DOS calculations with an open-source code. Conceptual difficulty is moderate due to careful slab construction and Hubbard U handling. Execution involves a multi-step pipeline of several DFT calculations with dependencies.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Slabs contain up to ~120 atoms, plane-wave cutoff 400 eV; DFT+U relaxations are feasible on modest CPU clusters. Memory demand is moderate (few GB per process), and input data (crystal structure, pseudopotentials) is negligible.
